The sixth beta of macOS 27 Golden Gate Bridge released today adds a new Golden Gate Bridge dynamic wallpaper, bringing the total to five dynamic wallpapers. All of them can be downloaded below.

macOS 27 Golden Gate Bridge wallpaper gallery keeps growing

When Apple unveiled macOS 27 Golden Gate Bridge at WWDC26, it showcased the same system wallpaper across all its operating systems, featuring a stylized "27" number as its theme.

However, after a few developer betas, Apple began adding dynamic screensavers that can also double as wallpapers, featuring stunning slow-motion footage overlooking San Francisco's iconic Golden Gate Bridge.

When the Mac is unlocked, the screensaver gradually slows down until it pauses, and each time it pauses, a fresh, slightly different wallpaper is left behind.

Although the dynamic effect is handled by macOS, below is a gallery of static stills from the four videos, as well as light and dark versions of the generic stylized "27" wallpaper.

Be sure to click on the images and save the full-resolution versions. To set one as your background, go to System Settings > Wallpaper, scroll down to "Your Photos," click the "Add Photos" button, and then do any of the following:

Add photos from your Photos library: Click "Choose from Photos," then select a photo. Add image files: Click "Choose Files," select the files, then click "Open." You can also drag images from your desktop or a folder onto the thumbnail at the top of the wallpaper settings. Add folders from Finder: Click "Choose Folder," select the folder, then click "Open." Add albums or folders from the Photos app: Select an album or folder under "Collections."

According to Apple, "You can also choose a custom wallpaper without opening wallpaper settings":

Use a photo from your Photos library: Go to the Photos app, select a photo, click the share button in the Photos toolbar, then click "Set as Wallpaper." Use an image found online: Control-click the image in a Safari window, then choose "Use Image as Desktop Wallpaper." Use an image stored on your Mac: Click the Finder icon in the Dock to open a Finder window. Control-click the image file, then click "Set as Desktop Picture."

To learn more about setting a custom wallpaper in macOS, visit this link.

Do you have a favorite? Let us know in the comments.
